newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian opposition starts boycott of parliament.
newsitem.headline: Austrian opposition starts boycott of parliament.

text.p: Austrian opposition parties began an unprecedented boycott of parliament on Tuesday, as a last resort to try to force an inquiry into the 1989 slaying of Kurdish dissidents in Vienna by suspected Iranian assassins.
In an extraordinary move Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party, the Liberals and leftist Greens last week announced they would unite to block all committee proceedings at least until June 10.

The parties want an independent inquiry into allegations that ministers at the time deliberately hindered a police investigation of the killing of Kurdish leader Abdorrahman Qasemlu and two other activists.

The coalition government of Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party, which holds a majority in the 183-seat assembly, has condemned the protest action as anti-democratic and insisted business would go on as usual.

Former Iranian president Abolhassan Bani-Sadr and a former top official at the Austrian foreign ministry have thrown their weight behind the issue, saying the government bowed to pressure from Iran by allowing the suspected killers to flee.

The government says its own report on the handling of the Kurdish affair, published two weeks ago, exonerates the then ministers of the accusations, although it admits Iran did try to intervene in the affair.
The opposition and domestic media have slammed the paper and called it a whitewash.
Meetings of five parliamentary committees and two under-committees were scheduled for Tuesday.
